- Dynamic Multi-step Planning
      - Multi-source Inconsistency
Run a readiness-and-conflict normalization pass only for live corporate
programs that are not yet finished or abandoned, but do not treat every
live record equally. The first attention goes to planning-stage items
that already have enough operating context in place to be actioned
now—meaning the venue side, reservation side, external partner side,
run-of-show side, and funding side already exist in some usable form.
Anything still merely conceptual or already closed should stay out of
scope unless it is only being checked so that an issue tied to an unread
operational alert can be reviewed and then acknowledged. Do not force
every planning record into a launch-ready condition. Where a provisional
place reservation can truly be solidified, do so; where outside work is
still only floated, finalize it only when the partner is active and
strong enough for the work expected; where a legitimate partner function
has no matching funding bucket yet, add the missing financial line
first; and where the run sheet is still in draft, move it through the
decision flow until it is cleared for handoff into execution readiness.
However, if a planning item is blocked because its provisional place
hold cannot actually be converted, or because its run sheet already sits
in a rejected state that cannot go back through the decision path, stop
short of artificial completion: verify the blocker, leave the record
short of full readiness, and then acknowledge the related unread
operational alert after that review. Unread operational alerts are not
to be swept up in bulk. Only acknowledge one when the underlying issue
connected to it has actually been examined during this cleanup. Re-check
the linked operational picture each time before closing the alert: the
core program record, place reservation situation, partner commitments,
spending effect, run-sheet condition, and any related messages must line
up with one another. For programs already in execution, unresolved
conflicts should not be left hanging. If a floated outside-work
commitment is invalid because the partner is inactive or fails the
qualification bar, terminate that floated commitment instead of leaving
it open. Then replace it with an appropriate active local partner when
needed; if none exists in the system for that local requirement, add one
and use it; and only lock in the replacement when the funding situation
can support it. Also, when the run-sheet history is internally
contradictory, formally settle the inconsistency by refusing the
still-waiting version rather than leaving a pending contradiction on the
record. A few records will matter more than the others during this pass
even though you should still review the full active set. One planning
record must complete the entire readiness chain if its facts support it:
EVT003. Another planning record should be pushed as far toward readiness
as the facts permit, even if not every surrounding dependency can be
perfected in the same way: EVT012. A different planning record must
explicitly remain unforced if its blockers are real, with only
review-and-acknowledgment of the related unread operational issue after
verification: EVT008. Among executing records, EVT013 is the one where
both the outside-work conflict and the contradictory run-sheet state
must be closed out rather than left open. When handling planning work,
let the causal sequence be driven by business logic rather than
convenience: a provisional place hold can only be treated as settled if
it can be settled; floated partner work should only become firm after
suitability is checked; any missing financial support line needed for a
partner function must exist before firming that work when such a line is
absent; and draft run sheets should end in a cleared state only if
eligible to proceed. When the opposite is true—failed reservation
conversion or a non-resubmittable rejected run sheet—review, preserve
the blocker, and acknowledge only the matching unread operational alert.
When handling execution conflicts, don’t just remove bad data and stop.
End the invalid floated partner work, source a geographically suitable
active replacement locally if one exists, otherwise introduced into the
records and then used, and the replacement should be made firm only when
funding still supports it. In parallel, if the run-sheet trail shows
contradiction between prior decisions and a still-waiting version,
resolve that contradiction decisively by refusing the waiting version.
Throughout the pass, cross-check the main record with its place
reservation, external work commitments, financial effect, run-sheet
standing, and linked operational alerts so each acted-on live program
ends in a verified closed workflow state for the issues addressed,
without needing any follow-up question from the user.
